buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 50% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 50 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 50 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 50 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Generic 1. The Seller shall not assign the Contract in whole or part without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 2. The Seller shall not sub-contract the Contract in whole or part to any entity without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 3. The Seller shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally liable and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due performance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under.

3. Generic Bidder financial standing: The bidder should not be under liquidation, court receivership or similar proceedings, should not be bankrupt. Bidder to upload undertaking to this effect with bid. 4. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 5. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Vehicle Specifications & Scope of Service (1) The agency must provide Sedan AC vehicles (such as Swift Dzire, Maruti Suzuki Dzire, Honda Amaze, T ata Tigor, Hyundai Aura/Xcent, or similar) to this office on a monthly basis as well as an 'On-Call' basi s. Priority will be given to CNG-powered vehicles. (2) The agency must provide vehicle facility on-call in a timely manner as per the demand of this office, an d vehicle services must be made available 24×7 hours. (3) In accordance with Letter No. S-10/GovtEmployee/Contract/Instruction/F/9 of the Commissioner of Heal th, Medical Services and Medical Education, Gandhinagar, no vehicle shall be assigned if it is register ed in the name of a government officer/employee, their spouse, children, or family members, or any person serving in a government office on a permanent, contractual, or outsourced basis. (4) Offices other than this office cannot utilize this vehicle service tender contract without the prior appro val of the Honorable Director. (5) If the agency's performance is deemed unsatisfactory, the Honorable Director (SIHFW) reserves the fin al right to terminate the contract prior to the stipulated term without stating any reason. (6) To terminate the contract before the stipulated period, the agency must provide a one (01) month prio r written notice. (7) In the event of the death of the agency's owner, the contract shall be deemed terminated, and their le gal heirs shall have no right or claim. (8) The rate contract for the vehicle service shall remain valid for one year from the date of commenceme nt of services. (9) All vehicles provided by the agency must have RTO passing dated after 01/04/2023. Additionally, all ve hicles must have traveled within a total limit of 1,000,000 km. (10) The bidder/agency must have an average annual turnover exceeding Rs. 10 Lakhs, and must mandat orily submit CA-certified turnover certificates for the last three financial years (2023-24, 2024-25, 20 25-26). 2. Operational Guidelines & Breakdown Management (11) In unforeseen circumstances, vehicles must be made available on holidays if required. If a vehicle br eaks down unexpectedly, the agency must arrange an alternative replacement vehicle within one (0 1) hour. If any such failure comes to notice after awarding the contract, the contract shall be cancelle d. (12) This contract is non-transferable. The agency cannot engage sub-agencies nor transfer this work to a ny other agency without the prior approval of the competent authority/office. (13) If the agency fails to render satisfactory service and the office is dissatisfied, the agency's contract wi ll be cancelled, and services will be procured from the L2 party (next to L1) at L1 rates. (14) For the vehicles provided to the office, any usage above or below the fixed baseline of 2,500 km per vehicle can be adjusted/balanced over a quarterly period (3 months). Quarterly calculations will be: J anuary to March, April to June, July to September, and October to December. (15) The model of the rented vehicle must be within the last three years and in excellent running conditio n. If the office finds a vehicle unsuitable, a replacement vehicle must be provided. (16) Vehicles provided on hire must be registered as passenger cars with the RTO under relevant laws an d must possess comprehensive insurance. Before starting rental services, copies of the Registration

Book (RC), Driving License, Insurance, Road Tax, Permit Book, etc. must be submitted and presented whenever demanded by this office for inspection. (17) Along with details of hired vehicles, complete details of standby vehicles and drivers must be submitt ed by the agency. 3. Penalties for Service Delay & Unauthorized Changes (18) The agency must provide vehicles punctually according to orders and instructions from the competen t officer or authorized representative. If a vehicle arrives late without prior approval, fails to arrive, b reaks down during duty, or if a driver/vehicle is changed without prior written permission from this office, the following penalties will be levied: Nature of Violation / Duration Penalty Amount Delay / Violation per Full Day Rs. 750/- per day Delay / Violation for Half Day Rs. 350/- for half day Delay per Hour Rs. 100/- per hour 4. Maintenance, Expenses & Financial Regulations (19) Two days of leave per month per vehicle will be adjusted on holidays according to convenience, duri ng which a standby vehicle must be arranged. The agency must conduct vehicle repairs and mainten ance during this period, which is binding on the agency. (20) Vehicle usage calculation will be based on the exact time and location where travel commences and ends. (21) The agency shall be solely responsible for compliance with Labor Laws, Sales Tax/GST, Income Tax, a nd other applicable statutory laws during the contract period. (22) Vehicles provided will be inspected periodically by responsible officers of this office. If vehicle conditi on is found unsatisfactory, a replacement vehicle must be assigned. (23) Vehicle hire rates include vehicle charges and driver arrangements. Fuel and operational expenses m ust be arranged by the agency at its own cost and risk. All expenses including maintenance, insuranc e, driver allowances, RTO taxes, salaries, and statutory taxes must be borne by the agency. Full resp onsibility for transport, maintenance, and repairs lies with the agency. This office holds no financial li ability beyond paying agreed rates for daily usage/kilometer travel. The agency bears complete liabili ty for accidents, loss, theft, vandalism, fire, or natural disasters during government duty; no compens ation or liability shall attach to this office. (24) A Logbook will be provided for recording vehicle usage, wherein entries regarding location, time, and distance (km) must be attested by the user officer. (25) Monthly bills accompanied by verified true copies of the logbook must be submitted to the competent officer. Upon verification of travel accuracy, payment authorization will be issued within 15 days by t he Accounts Branch, subject to statutory deductions (Income Tax, penalties, etc.). (26) Agencies agreed to provide vehicles under these conditions must deposit a Security Deposit equal to 3% of the total tender amount per vehicle via Demand Draft as per Gujarat State Procurement Policy – 2024. The deposit will be refunded after completion of the contract rules and carries no interest. Ou tstanding penalties or recovery amounts for contract breach may be deducted directly from the secu rity deposit. (27) In case of disputes regarding vehicle hire, the decision of the Director (SIHFW) shall be final and bindi ng. Legal jurisdiction shall strictly be Vadodara. 5. Driver Qualifications, Conduct & Safety Standards

(28) Vehicles provided by the agency must be equipped with a fully stocked First Aid Box in proper conditi on. (29) The agency shall not frequently change vehicles or drivers unless instructed by this office. (30) All bills must clearly specify the driver's name and vehicle registration number. (31) The agency must provide an authorized driver in proper uniform on a full-time (24-hour) basis. (32) Drivers supplied with vehicles must possess at least 3 years of driving experience in Government/No n-Government sectors and hold a valid Heavy Vehicle badge/license. (33) Drivers must strictly adhere to rules of discipline and courtesy. Drivers must be completely free from addictions such as bidi, cigarettes, gutkha/tobacco, and alcohol. (34) When traveling with female officers or staff on tour, the driver bears complete responsibility for their safety. (35) If a deployed driver is found unsuitable by this office, the agency must immediately replace the drive r with another person for duty. (36) Any damage or loss caused by any act of the driver during travel must be fully indemnified by the ag ency. (37) Drivers must regularly maintain the logbook and commence duty only after verification/confirmation by the officer in charge before travel starts. (38) The agency shall be liable to compensate for any direct or indirect damage caused to government pr operty due to driver incompetence, negligence, or intentional acts. Upon receiving any complaint reg arding driver irresponsibility or misconduct, the agency must replace the driver immediately. (39) The agency must verify the background history, character, personal details, and police verification re ports of all drivers before deployment. Only verified and suitable personnel shall be deputed as driver s. 6. Administrative & Final Provisions (40) Regarding vehicle requirements for other branches/offices of the Health Department under this rate c ontract, administrative and payment orders shall be issued directly by respective branches/offices wi thin their financial sanction limits and notified directly to the agency. (41) After entering into the rate contract, whenever this office requires vehicle services during the contrac t period, the agency must provide vehicles as per terms and adjust fleet size up or down according to requirement. (42) The Director, State Institute of Health and Family Welfare (SIHFW), Vadodara, holds absolute authorit y to terminate this contract at any time for breach of any of the above terms and conditions. . 6.
